clusters.trigger: A strings.json diff removes an existing key and adds the same content under a different key name, rather than only adding new keys.
clusters.rationale: Translations are keyed by name in the external translation platform, so a rename throws away work contributed in every language.

clusters.rule: Do not expose one translated enum state per vendor error code; collapse variants that are not individually actionable for the user into a single shared state.
clusters.trigger: A strings.json or enum diff adds many near-identical state values distinguished only by a device error number.
clusters.rationale: Each state has to be translated into every language and shown in the UI, for a distinction the user can do nothing with.

clusters.rule: Register push-update listeners in async_added_to_hass unconditionally via async_on_remove; do not hasattr-guard the subscription call to paper over an imprecise attribute type.
clusters.trigger: async_added_to_hass wraps add_update_listener or a similar subscription in an `if hasattr(...)` while sibling platforms in the same integration register it unconditionally.
clusters.rationale: The guard silently produces an entity that never updates when the attribute type is wrong, instead of failing where the type can be fixed.

clusters.rule: Config entry and subentry migrations must preserve any value the user already has, defaulting a new option only when its key is absent.
clusters.trigger: async_migrate_entry or async_update_subentry writes a data dict where the new default is spread after the existing data and overwrites it.
clusters.rationale: The migration runs on every existing install, so an ordering mistake silently resets settings users deliberately changed.

clusters.rule: Raise ConfigEntryError, ConfigEntryNotReady, ConfigEntryAuthFailed and HomeAssistantError with translation_domain and translation_key plus a matching exceptions entry in strings.json, not a hard-coded English message.
clusters.trigger: An integration raises one of these exceptions with a literal English string argument.
clusters.rationale: These messages are shown directly in the UI, so they have to go through the translation system like every other user-facing string.

clusters.rule: Trigger, condition and action YAML target selectors must list every domain the feature applies to, including the matching input_* helper domain.
clusters.trigger: A triggers.yaml / conditions.yaml / services.yaml target entity selector names a single domain where the corresponding helper domain (input_select, input_boolean, input_number, ...) also implements the behavior.
clusters.rationale: The selector is what the automation editor offers, so an omitted helper domain hides working functionality from the UI.

clusters.rule: Device-quirk workarounds must not be added to a core entity base class without an architecture proposal that pins down the exact semantics - thresholds, drift windows, resulting behaviour.
clusters.trigger: A diff adds normalization or heuristic logic, such as an uptime normalizer with an implicit tolerance, to an entity base class in homeassistant/components/<domain>/__init__.py.
clusters.rationale: A heuristic in the base class silently changes behaviour for every integration on that domain, so the numbers have to be agreed rather than chosen in a PR.

clusters.rule: New entity service or command implementations such as play_media and browse_media need behaviour tests that call them; a snapshot-only platform test is not sufficient coverage.
clusters.trigger: A platform gains async_play_media/async_browse_media or other command methods while tests/components/<domain>/ only contains snapshot assertions.
clusters.rationale: Snapshots assert the entities exist, never that calling them does the right thing, so the whole new code path is untested.

clusters.rule: Do not report fabricated progress values from an update entity; omit in_progress and update_percentage when the device does not expose a real percentage.
clusters.trigger: An UpdateEntity property returns hard-coded percentages derived from a status enum rather than a device-reported number.
clusters.rationale: A made-up percentage that sits still or jumps is worse than no progress bar, because the user reads it as real.

clusters.rule: Mappings derived from device capability data must be rebuilt when used, or refreshed on update events, not computed once in __init__.
clusters.trigger: An entity caches a dict built from device status or capabilities in __init__ and a service method reads that cache with a slugify or raw fallback when the key is missing.
clusters.rationale: Capabilities change while the entity lives - sources appear, inputs are renamed - so a cache built at construction time silently goes stale and the fallback hides it.

clusters.rule: Do not change the value of an existing entity state or state attribute, for example by slugifying it; keep the raw value and add a map from API keys to Home Assistant translation keys for display.
clusters.trigger: A diff wraps a previously exposed attribute value in slugify()/lower()/a rename, changing what the attribute reports for existing installs.
clusters.rationale: Users template and compare on those exact values in automations, so changing them breaks working configurations with no warning.
